To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the transnational literary field is structured in three clusters: (a) authors with no recognition, (b) authors who receive recognition from other agents in their own country but not from the international literary field, and (c) authors who receive international recognition from the international literary elite.

(1) in the literary field, institutional recognition in the transnational literary field is characterized by three distinct clusters, which are related to symbolic capital, (2) the composition of the clusters differs across countries, but (3) the patterns of recognition are highly similar in local and international recognition.

(a) in all countries, three clusters are consistently present: the historical prestigious, contemporary prestigious and the unrecognized; (b) the historical prestigious cluster is most strongly represented in French newspaper literary coverage; (c) the contemporary prestigious cluster is most prominent in the German newspaper literary coverage; and (d) the unrecognized cluster is most strongly present in US newspaper literary coverage.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
institutional recognition is a transnational process that is increasingly de-hierarchized, and that it is related to the symbolic capital of the author.
the literary field has become increasingly de-hierarchized in the past fifty years, but that this de-hierarchizing process has been more pronounced in some countries than in others.
institutional recognition is not a zero-sum game, but a game with a limited number of winners.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the institutional recognition of fiction authors in newspapers is a highly stable and transnational process.
institutional recognition is a complex, multi-layered and multi-dimensional process that cannot be reduced to the simple presence or absence of recognition in a single institution.
the institutionalization of literature is a process in which local and transnational forces are intertwined.
